2002=2\cdot7\cdot11\cdot13,
it suffices by the Chinese Remainder Theorem to prove periodicity modulo each prime p\in\{2,7,11,13\}.

Write 2002 in base p. The numbers of base-p digits are respectively
11,4,4,3.
Thus 2002<p^{L_p}, where
L_2=11,\quad L_7=L_{11}=4,\quad L_{13}=3.

By Lucas' theorem, \binom{n}{2002}\pmod p depends only on the first L_p base-p digits of n, because 2002 has no nonzero digits at positions \ge L_p. Adding p^{L_p} to n leaves those lower L_p digits unchanged. Therefore
\[
\binom{n+p^{L_p}}{2002}\equiv \binom{n}{2002}\pmod p
\]
for every n\ge2002. Hence the sequence is periodic modulo each p, with periods 2^{11},7^4,11^4,13^3.

\[
\operatorname{lcm}(2^{11},7^4,11^4,13^3)=2^{11}7^4 11^4 13^3.

2002=2\cdot7\cdot11\cdot13.

It is enough to establish periodicity modulo each of these primes.

For a prime p, let L_p be the number of digits in the base-p expansion of 2002. Directly,
\[
2002=11111010010_2=5560_7=1560_{11}=BB0_{13},
\]
where B denotes 11. Hence
\[
L_2=11,\qquad L_7=L_{11}=4,\qquad L_{13}=3.
\]

\[
a_{n+p^{L_p}}\equiv a_n\pmod p
\]
for all n\ge2002. Thus a_n is periodic modulo every prime divisor of 2002.

Taking the least common multiple of the four periods yields a period modulo 2002:
\[
T=\operatorname{lcm}(2^{11},7^4,11^4,13^3)=2^{11}7^4 11^4 13^3.
\]

outputs.final_proof:
Let
\[
a_n=\binom{n}{2002}\qquad(n\ge2002).
\]
We prove that a common period exists modulo 2002.

The prime factorization is
\[
2002=2\cdot7\cdot11\cdot13.
\]
It is therefore sufficient to find a period modulo each prime factor.

For p\in\{2,7,11,13\}, let L_p be the number of digits of 2002 in base p. The expansions are
\[
2002=11111010010_2=5560_7=1560_{11}=BB0_{13},
\]
so
\[
(L_2,L_7,L_{11},L_{13})=(11,4,4,3).
\]
Since 2002<p^{L_p}, its base-p digits at positions L_p and above are zero. Lucas' theorem consequently implies that \binom{n}{2002} modulo p depends only on the lowest L_p base-p digits of n. These digits are unchanged when n is replaced by n+p^{L_p}. Hence
\[
a_{n+p^{L_p}}\equiv a_n\pmod p
\]
for every n\ge2002.

Thus the sequence is periodic modulo each prime with respective periods
\[
2^{11},\quad7^4,\quad11^4,\quad13^3.
\]
Taking their least common multiple gives
\[
T=\operatorname{lcm}(2^{11},7^4,11^4,13^3)=2^{11}7^4 11^4 13^3.
\]
For every n, the difference a_{n+T}-a_n is divisible by each of 2,7,11,13, and hence by their product 2002. Therefore a_{n+T}\equiv a_n\pmod{2002}, proving periodicity.
